newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares dive 2.77 pct on political fears.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares dive 2.77 pct on political fears.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell sharply in thin trade on Monday morning as the market remained haunted by concerns over the fate of the Islamist-led coalition government, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 ended 40 points, or 2.77 percent lower at 1,403. Morning volume dropped further to 3.02 trillion lira from Friday's 3.65 trillion.
Brokers said political worries continued to hinder liquidity inflow to the market and depressed volume.
Former minister Yalim Erez stepped up his campaign late last week to forge a secularist alliance to replace Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's divided coalition.

Erez, from the coalition's conservative wing, had been trying to build support for a secularist pact since he resigned in late April over the ruling Islamists' reluctance to comply with army demands for a crackdown on rising Islamist activism.
About 100,000 demonstrators protested at a planned clampdown on Islamic schools in Istanbul over the weekend.

The powerful secularist army has ordered compulsory secular education be increased to eight years from five as part of the measures. Islamists say this will effectively shut down the middle section of state religious schools which now take pupils at age 11.

Of the 248 shares traded, falls outdid rises sharply by 200 to 18 and 30 ended steady. The IMKB Industrial shed 2.38 percent to 1,396, the IMKB Services lost 2.44 percent to 1,279 and the IMKB Financial dived 3.12 percent to 1,524.
